text: AI agents can pick up skills: reusable instructions for a task. Here is a new paper about how they find the right one.
Open-source collections of skills have now grown past two hundred thirty thousand.
So the hard part is no longer writing a skill. It is choosing which one to use.
A common fix lets a language model search, refine, and search again. Every task pays for that loop.
SkillSeek uses plain retrieval instead. A fast bi-encoder shortlists skills, then a cross-encoder re-ranks them.
On SkillsBench, a benchmark of eighty-nine tasks, it matches the language model approaches.
Even plain BM25 keyword search matches the refined loops in three of four settings.
The cost per trial drops from fifty-one dollars thirty to twenty-seven dollars fifty-four. The no-skill baseline is about twenty-seven.
The takeaway: start with classic retrieval, and bring in a language model only when it falls short.
The paper is SkillSeek, on arXiv. Thanks for watching.
